clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old Chinese male chef presented with six-month history of foamuria and progressive generalized edema, accompanied by diffuse refractory verrucous hyperplasia on limbs and face prominent on feet (history of verruca vulgaris since age 29). Initial workup confirmed nephrotic syndrome (24-hour urine protein 4.5 g, serum albumin 16.5 g/L, microscopic hematuria) with positive ANA (1:100), elevated anti-dsDNA (25.4 IU), and hypocomplementemia (C3 0.58 g/L). Renal biopsy in November 2022 established the diagnosis of class V lupus nephritis. Concurrent immunologic evaluation revealed severe CD4 lymphocytopenia (77 cells/µL, reference 441-2156/µL) with normal CD8 counts and negative HIV testing (as well as negative hepatitis B, C, EBV, CMV, syphilis), meeting criteria for idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia (ICL) and explaining the refractory, widespread HPV-related skin lesions. The patient was treated with belimumab added to standard therapy; after one year, renal function improved with partial remission of proteinuria, subdued lupus activity, and stable warts, despite CD4+ T-cell counts remaining persistently below 150 cells/µL throughout the disease course.
